reporting_accuracy_2026_08_03.defect_1_identity: Every people-count was count(DISTINCT distinct_id). PostHog issues a new distinct_id per anonymous device and aliases it onto a person_id on sign-in, reinstall or restore. 348 ids across 297 actual people; one person carries 27 ids alone, another 14, another 11. Installs inflated 17%, so every conversion rate divided by them was understated, and each phantom id looks like a one-visit never-returner, which is how a returning buyer vanishes from the active count in the week they paid. Fixed: m_installs, m_active, m_activation, m_funnel, m_retention all count person_id, guarded by a test that reads the query source.
reporting_accuracy_2026_08_03.defect_2_plants: capturePlantAdded is called from exactly one place, lib/features/plants/screens/plant_form_screen.dart:596. purchase_telemetry_defect.what: A completed sale can be recorded as a dismissal. 1 of our 3 production sales is recorded that way in PostHog right now.
purchase_telemetry_defect.mechanism: paywall_screen.dart:213 awaits service.purchasePackage(...), line 217 then does 'if (!mounted) return;'. The await runs up to 8s inside waitForEntitlement (entitlement_service.dart:470) against a 10s call timeout. Dispose in that window and neither capturePurchaseSucceeded nor _fireResult runs, so dispose() at line 89 fires 'dismissed' because _resultFired is still false.
purchase_telemetry_defect.second_path: case PurchaseOutcome.cancelled: break; at line 251 fires nothing at all, so a genuine cancel and a dropped sale are indistinguishable.

purchase_telemetry_defect.ticket: DAL-237, retitled from "instrument paywall views" (work already done) to the defect, description rewritten, Todo, assigned to Benedict.
purchase_telemetry_defect.fix_part_1: Fire the purchase events from inside EntitlementService.purchasePackage rather than the widget callback, and give cancelled its own outcome value. Small, no privacy implications, Benedict commits it.
purchase_telemetry_defect.fix_part_2: Push the PostHog distinct id to RevenueCat as a subscriber attribute at configure time so anonymous buyers are attributable. Benedict's privacy call, deliberately separate.
purchase_telemetry_defect.consequence: Every paywall dismissal rate we have quoted is an upper bound, and PostHog purchase counts are a lower bound. RevenueCat remains the source of truth for money.

query_movement_thresholds.decision: DEC-327 / DAL-268 (2026-08-27). The consequence ticket after DAL-261 fixed the truncation.
query_movement_thresholds.finding: The daily email's 'position movers' block was noise, and the truncation fix made that visible rather than causing it. Old rule: moved 5+ spots, NO impression floor, sorted by size of move, top 10. ~316 qualifying rows/week, 45% of them queries that vanished from GSC entirely the next week, 31% held. Of the rows actually PRINTED the median had 1 impression and 98% had <=2 in both weeks.
query_movement_thresholds.why_structural: Sorting by size of move selects the extreme tail, and the extreme tail of a position distribution is wherever the data is thinnest. The block was guaranteed to print the least reliable rows available.
query_movement_thresholds.noise_floor_measured: Median absolute week-over-week position swing by min impressions across both weeks, 8 windows 2026-06-30..2026-08-24: 1-2 impr n=4192 median 4.0 p90 26.0 and 45% move >=5; 3-9 n=1186 median 2.2 p90 12.9; 10-29 n=231 median 1.4 p90 8.7; 30+ n=15 median 0.5. At 1-2 impressions the MEDIAN query moves 4 spots doing nothing.
query_movement_thresholds.the_broken_dial_was_the_floor_not_the_sp: Backtested on whether the move was still there a week later. No floor + 15 spots = 131 rows/wk, 50% vanished, 27% held (WORSE than the old rule). Floor 5 + 5 spots = 27 rows/wk, 2% vanished, 54% held. Floor 5 + 10 spots = 10 rows/wk, 2% vanished, 51% held. Raising the spot threshold alone made it worse; the floor did all the work.
query_movement_thresholds.shipped: MOVER_MIN_IMPRESSIONS = 5 (in BOTH weeks), MOVER_MIN_SPOTS = 10 (one clear of the 10-29 band p90 of 8.7), NEW_QUERY_MIN_IMPRESSIONS = 5, and movers sorted by impressions not by change. tools/autonomous/traffic_report.py, deployed.

closed_store_answering_200.decision: DEC-330 (2026-08-27). Emergency exception, shipped ff036ce, deployed and verified from /opt/dale/scrapers.
closed_store_answering_200.what: Heritage Fruit Trees shut online sales for 2026 on 08-24. It 503ed for two nights (guard working), then from 08-26 began answering HTTP 200 with the whole catalogue present, every product OutOfStock and unpriced: 378 products, 0 in stock, 1 priced. ok=true reset consecutive_failures to 0, so the dormancy guard shipped 08-24 could never fire and Heritage was being scraped nightly until the 2027 season.
closed_store_answering_200.cost_was_real: Runs got LONGER not shorter (432s on the last real day, then 1235s and 1245s) because a 503 fails fast and a 200 does not. ~20 min/night of pointless requests at a nursery Benedict has a relationship with. Scraping cost goodwill twice: Beewise (DEC-198) and Heaven On Earth, who threatened Consumer Affairs the same day.
closed_store_answering_200.not_a_data_defect: Checked the far end (DEC-270) before building a repair. The live page really serves HTTP 200 with schema.org/OutOfStock and no price. The scraper is CORRECT, Heritage genuinely has nothing buyable, and the published CC BY dataset is not lying. untrusted_nurseries() is deliberately UNTOUCHED: marking Heritage untrusted would suppress a zero that is true. The fix changes whether we scrape, never whether we believe.
closed_store_answering_200.fix: is_unproductive(rec) = ok AND products>0 AND in_stock==0 AND priced share < UNPRODUCTIVE_PRICED_SHARE (0.10). consecutive_failures and last_success_day count those alongside outright failures.
closed_store_answering_200.priced_condition_is_load_bearing: A nursery can sell out completely and still trade, and a trading store keeps its prices on the page (~100% priced). Withdrawing prices too is what separates 'closed' from 'sold out', and it protects the restock alerts that are the reason to scrape daily. Heritage is 1/378 = 0.3% against a 10% threshold.
closed_store_answering_200.base_rate_measured_not_chosen: Across 27 nurseries and 200 days of health records, ok runs with products>0 and in_stock==0 occurred EXACTLY TWICE, both Heritage on 08-26 and 08-27. Zero false positives in all history.
closed_store_answering_200.threshold_not_bent: Streak reads 4 today; 5 is required. One more unproductive night is still needed before it sleeps, so the constant was not tuned to make today's case fire today (DEC-323).
closed_store_answering_200.the_alarm_could_not_see_it: detect_scrape_anomalies.py gained a priced_collapse rule on 08-24, two days before this. It compares today's priced share to YESTERDAY'S, and yesterday (08-25) was a failure carrying no priced field, so the comparison was skipped; on 08-27 today equalled yesterday so nothing fired. The alarm built for this exact failure was structurally unable to see it because the collapse happened ACROSS an outage. Same family as DEC-325. Not fixed here (backlog at cap); belongs to DAL-292.
closed_store_answering_200.guard: 6 new tests in tests/test_dormancy.py: the exact production sequence, the sold-out-but-trading case that must NOT back off, pre-priced records that must never be judged retroactively, and that an unproductive run stays TRUSTED data. Proven to fail 3/3 under the old logic before being trusted to pass (DEC-326). Full suite 3,565 OK.
